title.narrative: Pathways to resilient livelihoods of indigenous people in Ratanakiri Province, Cambodia

description.narrative: Overall objective = The food and nutrition security of indigenous communities in Ratanakiri Province is sustainably improved.Project objective = 610 indigenous households (3,050 people) in four districts in Ratanakiri have a solid livelihood, with a focus on securing food, income and land rights.For indigenous households to have resilient livelihoods that focus on securing food, income, and land rights, household-level agricultural production needs to be improved and diversified. This project focuses on improving the agricultural production of cashew nuts, including through the installment or improvement of cashew nut processing centres, enabling farmers increase the value of their cashews. In addition, when nutrition knowledge and awareness is improved and practiced at household level, then household diets will improve, particularly the nutritional intake of women. Finally, the project has a focus on supporting communities to gain community land titles (CLTs), providing lasting legal protection for community lands, including farmland and forests; land which communities rely on for their livelihoods and thus food security.

The target group is from 23 indigenous communities (total population 13,201) in four districts of Ratanakiri. The target group belong to Kavet, Prov, Kreung, Charay, Lun, and Kachok indigenous groups. All communities (except one) are from the P5424 project. One new community, Krala in Ou Chum district has been added because of its suitability for the development a cashew nut processing centre. The direct target group are 610 indigenous farmers and their households. The intervention consists of focused activities related to different outputs in the same communities. The activities will be implemented through a ‘group approach’, such as nutrition groups, saving groups, cashew nut processing groups or water user committees and communal land title committees. Women’s participation in the committees will be emphasized as a means of promoting gender transformation. The indirect target group are circa 13, 200 persons living in the 23 communities that do not participate in activities but will benefit from the community level activities. Other indirect target groups are groups and individuals the project collaborates with, for example local authorities and government staff, and staff of other NGOs/ networks.

This project works to sustainably improve the food and nutrition security of indigenous communities in Ratanakiri, targeting 610 indigenous households (3,050 people) in four districts. It does this through three main outputs, supporting 460 female farmers in 23 communities to have improved and diversified home garden production and 6 schools to have improved/ diversified vegetable production, benefitting 150 cashew nut farmers (60 f, 90 m) through improved cashew value chains as a result of 3 cashew nut processing centers, and strengthening the capacity of indigenous community groups to engage in community issues such as land rights, NRM, and conservation.
